title: Microsoft Film Studio: Box Office Market Intelligence & ML Engine
summary: Executive consulting study and machine learning suite combining box office financial analytics, Random Forest revenue prediction (R²=0.74), and NLP critic sentiment mining (AUC=0.81).
description:
When Microsoft leadership evaluated entering the original video content market alongside tech industry peers, they required empirical market intelligence and predictive analytics to navigate an unfamiliar domain. This project delivers an end-to-end data science consultation paired with active Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing models.

To overcome severe missing-data limitations in baseline public datasets, an advanced multi-source ETL pipeline was built. This included a custom JavaScript DOM auto-scroller and BeautifulSoup HTML parsing engine to scrape over 14,000 IMDbPro records, paired with REST API integration targeting TMDB to ingest popularity indices across 26,500+ movies.

Going beyond exploratory data analysis, the repository implements a Supervised Random Forest Regressor predicting worldwide box office gross (R²=0.74, MAE=$52M) based on production budgets, release timing, and genre combinations. Additionally, an NLP sentiment classifier trained on 54,400+ Rotten Tomatoes critic reviews uses TF-IDF vectorization and Logistic Regression (AUC=0.81) to predict review freshness and extract key thematic sentiment drivers.

title: King County Housing Price Prediction & Streamlit Micro-App
summary: Multivariate regression & gradient boosting framework (LightGBM R²=0.875) with an interactive Streamlit web micro-app estimating residential real estate values across King County, WA.
description:
In real estate markets, accurately valuing residential properties is critical for homebuyers, sellers, and financial underwriters. Using the King County House Sales dataset (~21,600 homes), this project combines classical OLS regression diagnostics with modern regularized regression (Ridge, Lasso) and Gradient Boosting (LightGBM) to deliver accurate price estimates (LightGBM R² = 0.875).

Features extensive EDA, Haversine spatial distance calculations to central Seattle, log-normal feature scaling, and Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) multicollinearity pruning. Paired with a live interactive Streamlit micro-app allowing recruiters to adjust property specs (living area sqft, grade, bedrooms, zipcode) and receive real-time price predictions.
highlights: Exploratory Data Analysis across 19 physical, temporal, and spatial features in Seattle & King County.
Engineered log-transformed continuous variables, one-hot encoded categorical factors, and Haversine distance metrics to central Seattle.
Multi-model benchmark comparing Statsmodels OLS, Ridge, Lasso, and LightGBM regressors.
Built a live interactive Streamlit web micro-app enabling real-time property price evaluations.

title: Pneumonia Detection from Chest X-Rays via Deep CNNs
summary: Automated diagnostic deep learning model evaluating lung X-ray scans using Convolutional Neural Networks to assist medical practitioners in identifying acute pneumonia infections.
description: Pneumonia is an infection that inflames air sacs in one or both lungs, affecting over 150 million people annually. This project leverages transfer learning and deep CNN architectures to classify pediatric and adult chest X-ray images into Normal vs. Pneumonia infected cases, achieving high recall and diagnostic accuracy.

title: FFT-Based Protein Docking & Binding Affinity Simulation
summary: Developed Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) binding affinity algorithms at Illinois Institute of Technology to evaluate protein complexes and streamline high-throughput docking simulations.
description: High-throughput computational protein-protein docking requires rapid grid-based electrostatic and shape-complementarity evaluation. Developed specialized FFT-accelerated Python algorithms to calculate binding affinities across large structural databases.

title: Facial Emotion Classification & E-Journaling App
summary: Transfer-learning Convolutional Neural Network trained to classify Paul Ekman’s 7 primary facial emotions (Angry, Disgust, Fear, Happy, Sad, Surprise, Neutral) for emotion tracking.
description: Facial expressions convey emotional states that picture journals and vlogs capture. Built a full-stack Django application integrating a Keras CNN with transfer learning to train, re-train, and log emotional states from webcams and uploaded images.

title: Retail Recommendation Engines & Consumer Sentiment NLP
summary: Supervised and unsupervised ML models built at Promoboxx, featuring campaign recommendation systems (XGBoost) and consumer sentiment NLP pipelines.
description: Architected end-to-end feature engineering pipelines, missing data imputation strategies, A/B testing evaluation frameworks, and XGBoost recommendation models for digital retail marketing campaigns alongside spaCy/NLTK sentiment analysis.

title: Ab Initio Quantum & Classical Simulations of Materials
summary: Ph.D. dissertation research at UMKC modeling structural, electronic, and mechanical properties of cement hydrates and intermetallic compounds.
description: Performed extensive quantum mechanical density functional theory (DFT) calculations using Quantum Espresso and VASP to model complex crystal structures, vibrational density of states, and high-temperature oxidation mechanisms.

title: Telecom Churn Risk Classifier & SHAP Diagnostic Engine
summary: XGBoost gradient boosting classifier with Optuna hyperparameter optimization (Recall=82.5%, ROC-AUC=0.865), TreeSHAP explainability diagnostics, and a live interactive Streamlit risk calculator.
description:
Predicting and mitigating customer churn is vital for telecommunication revenue retention. Using the Telco Customer Churn dataset (~7,040 customers), this project upgrades legacy baseline models to a modern XGBoost classification pipeline tuned with Optuna hyperparameter optimization.

To address severe class imbalance and prioritize high-risk retention targets, the pipeline optimizes directly for Recall and ROC-AUC (achieving 82.5% Recall on churners and 0.865 ROC-AUC). Integrated with SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to quantify individual feature contributions (such as contract commitment, monthly charges, and technical support add-ons). Paired with an interactive Streamlit micro-app allowing users to evaluate customer profiles in real time.
highlights: Upgraded 2020 baseline Random Forest model to an Optuna-tuned XGBoost gradient boosting classifier.
Achieved 82.5% Recall on churn class and 0.865 ROC-AUC across 5-fold cross validation.
Incorporated TreeSHAP beeswarm, waterfall, and dependence diagnostic plots explaining top retention drivers.
Built a live interactive Streamlit churn risk calculator web application with real-time SHAP explanations.
